title: LIVE VISIBILITY
noaa_source: NOAA/NCEP HRRR 3 km surface visibility analysis, hourly cycles
product_name: NOAA/NCEP HRRR 3 km surface visibility analysis, hourly cycles
variable: VIS surface analysis (meteorological visibility, not astronomical seeing)
spatial_resolution_source: ~3 km HRRR CONUS grid, mean-binned to the common canvas, despike-gated, continuity-filled, NaN-aware display smoothing
spatial_resolution_rendered: 1800x1175 canvas over lon [-93.0,-73.5], lat [40.5,49.5] (mean-value binning, no upsampling of source precision)
missing_data_treatment: only [0,200000] m admitted pre-conversion (ultra-clear Arctic air often exceeds 60 km; gating lower punched transparent holes in the clearest regions); sub-1-mile claims require RH>=90% (model-consistency despike); gated cells continuity-filled from surrounding valid values (valid pixels never altered; fraction in metadata); values above 30 mi clamp into deep blue; full basin rectangle, no shoreline cut; residual edge no-data transparent with anti-fringe RGB bleed; never zero-filled.
shoreline_mask: assets/great_lakes_watermask.png — shared NOAA medium-resolution shoreline water mask (nautical-chart compilation, mean-high-water datum; snapped + polygonized once, full vertex precision, antialiased). Overlay alpha is multiplied by this mask and edge RGB is bled into transparent pixels (anti-fringe for bilinear clients), so every product shares one shoreline.

legend_scale_html: Meteorological visibility in statute miles (HRRR surface analysis, FAA flight-category scale): 0-0.25 Dense fog maroon (NWS Dense Fog Advisory, 1/4 mi or less) → 0.25-1 LIFR red → 1-3 IFR orange → 3-5 MVFR gold → 5-30 VFR green to deep blue (10SM is the METAR reporting cap; the model resolves past it). Same visibility always shows the same color; above 30 mi clamps into deep blue. Human-observer/mariner/pilot visibility through haze, mist, precipitation, and smoke — not astronomical seeing.
folder_html:
Legend

Meteorological visibility in statute miles (HRRR surface analysis, FAA flight-category scale): 0-0.25 Dense fog maroon (NWS Dense Fog Advisory, 1/4 mi or less) → 0.25-1 LIFR red → 1-3 IFR orange → 3-5 MVFR gold → 5-30 VFR green to deep blue (10SM is the METAR reporting cap; the model resolves past it). Same visibility always shows the same color; above 30 mi clamps into deep blue. Human-observer/mariner/pilot visibility through haze, mist, precipitation, and smoke — not astronomical seeing.

Near-surface meteorological visibility from the operational HRRR analysis: how far a human observer, mariner, or pilot can distinguish surroundings through haze, mist, precipitation, and smoke. Low values flag navigation and shoreline hazards; high values mark crystal-clear Great Lakes air.

Visibility science (atmospheric optics and observing practice) quantifies horizontal contrast loss from scattering and absorption by hydrometeors and aerosols. It underpins aviation flight rules, marine navigation advisories, and air-quality perception, and is reported operationally in statute miles across the United States.

Units: mi, statute (display; source m / 1609.344)
